title: Family reunification plan with three meeting levels
summary: Use a nearby point, neighbourhood point, and out-of-area destination so the family has options when one zone is inaccessible.
content: Action sequence: Choose one safe point immediately outside the home, one outside the neighbourhood, and one outside the affected area. For each point write the trigger, route, transport, accessibility, animal policy, contact person, and waiting time. Agree that everyone sends status to one outside contact rather than repeatedly calling each other. Practise a weekday, night, school, and no-phone version of the plan. Safety boundary: Do not select a meeting point in a flood channel, dense vegetation, fuel area, unstable building, or traffic hazard. Do not keep changing the plan through separate messages; one person must own the current version.
steps: Choose one safe point immediately outside the home, one outside the neighbourhood, and one outside the affected area.
warnings: Do not select a meeting point in a flood channel, dense vegetation, fuel area, unstable building, or traffic hazard.

title: Rumour verification card during disasters
summary: Prevent false route, casualty, shelter, water, medicine, or weather information from driving unsafe decisions.
content: Action sequence: Write the exact claim, original source, publication time, location, and requested action. Check Civil Protection, 112 alerts, local authority, emergency services, utility provider, or another competent primary source. Mark the claim confirmed, false, outdated, location-specific, or unresolved. If it was shared, send a correction to the same recipients with the verified source and time. Safety boundary: Do not forward urgent-looking content merely because many people sent it. Do not reveal private identities or locations while correcting a rumour.

warnings: Do not forward urgent-looking content merely because many people sent it.

title: Missing household member information packet
summary: Prepare a factual packet for police, 112, responders, and trusted search coordinators without launching an unsafe informal search.
content: Action sequence: Record full name, age, appearance, clothing, phone, vehicle, mobility, communication, medical urgency, and any immediate hazard. Write the last confirmed time, exact location, source of confirmation, intended route, and usual destinations. Contact authorities promptly when risk is elevated and preserve messages, calls, transport records, and witness details. Assign one family contact to receive updates and prevent conflicting reports. Safety boundary: Do not enter floodwater, fire zones, unstable structures, cliffs, caves, or restricted terrain to search without trained coordination. Do not publish sensitive medical, identity, or location details more widely than necessary.

title: Neighbour check-in without creating dependency or confusion
summary: Coordinate brief consent-based checks for isolated or vulnerable neighbours while keeping clear limits and emergency escalation.
content: Action sequence: Ask in advance who wants a check, preferred method, emergency contact, access need, animal, medicine, or device concern. Use a fixed check window and a simple status: okay, needs practical help, needs qualified help, or no response. For no response, follow the agreed sequence of call, trusted contact, building manager or neighbour, and emergency service when risk justifies it. Record only necessary facts and close each request with a named next action. Safety boundary: Do not enter a home, handle medicine, move a person, or operate utilities beyond consent and training. Do not promise continuous monitoring that the group cannot reliably provide.

warnings: Do not enter a home, handle medicine, move a person, or operate utilities beyond consent and training.

title: Bilingual emergency notice for a shared building
summary: Post a short Greek-English notice with source, time, affected area, required action, assistance point, and next update.
content: Action sequence: Use a clear title such as EVACUATE, SHELTER INSIDE, WATER NOT SAFE, POWER HAZARD, or NEXT UPDATE. Write source, publication time, exact floors or areas, action, route, meeting point, accessibility help, contact, and next review time. Use large lettering, simple symbols, high contrast, and both Greek and English. Remove or cross out the notice visibly when it expires and replace it with a dated correction. Safety boundary: Do not invent an authority, instruction, shelter, or route. Do not leave an outdated notice in place after conditions change.
